one_line: Browser agents directly build and test live 3D game scenes.
what_it_does: Feather Engine exposes scene creation, physics, terrain, lighting, controllers, and play testing through WebMCP tools in a live Three.js/Rapier editor.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools materially change 3D scene manipulation: an agent can reliably create and configure spatial objects and physics instead of guessing through a dense visual editor.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 14 direct engine tools plus gateway tools for scene and gameplay operations.
Frame sheets show a live engine workspace and 3D viewport progression.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent engine/editor scope with populated controls and a live 3D viewport, though exact end-to-end agent invocation is not legible.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets show setup/editor states progressing to a 3D grid viewport.
Devpost packaging identifies a live demo and video titled Feather Engine + WebMCP.
impact_rationale: Game developers and prototypers have a credible need for faster scene setup and iterative testing; the product addresses costly spatial and physics authoring work.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets building scenes, configuring physics, and testing gameplay.
About text grounds the problem in manual Unity-style object placement and physics work.
creativity_rationale: A live browser-native 3D engine controlled through a structured agent surface is an ambitious and memorable WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Combines natural-language agent control with scene building, physics, vehicles, and live play mode.
Human undo/redo is integrated into the agent workflow.
usability_note: The visible editor is substantial but likely complex for first-time users.
red_flags: No readable tool-call transcript in frame sheets.
standouts: High-leverage agent control over a live 3D engine.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and ambitious, visibly real product scope.

one_line: A shared traceable 3D atlas for reasoning about smell and fragrance formulas.
what_it_does: Olfaria provides typed search, relation, comparison, path-finding, and focus tools over a live olfactory graph shared by person and agent.
leverage_rationale: Typed bounded graph operations avoid unreliable scraping and canvas interpretation while preserving a shared visual evidence surface.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies five typed tools for search, relations, comparisons, paths, and visual focus.
Frames show a populated circular atlas alongside structured analysis panels.
execution_rationale: The repeated atlas states and guided analysis views show a coherent, intentionally designed workflow, though calls and exact outputs are not directly legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show progression from welcome to populated atlas and structured prompt/result states.
Devpost screenshot includes an embedded WebMCP demo and live 3D workspace.
impact_rationale: Perfumer and formulation users have a real need to search ambiguous sensory language and retain traceable evidence; the fit is specific and credible.
impact_evidence: About text identifies perfumers and the difficulty of searching and explaining smell.
Corpus evidence is kept separate from formulation interpretation.
creativity_rationale: The concept of a shared, traceable olfactory knowledge space with agent-assisted graph traversal is unusually original and deeply matched to the medium.
creativity_evidence: Live 3D olfactory atlas is a distinctive shared human-agent interaction model.
Explicit uncertainty and provenance separation show depth beyond a generic chatbot.
usability_note: The atlas and structured panels appear thoughtfully designed, though smell-domain complexity remains high.
red_flags: Agent invocation is claimed but not directly readable in frames.
advance_reason: Excellent creative concept with strong WebMCP leverage and credible audience value.

one_line: A privacy-first browser toolbox where local models and outside agents use the same WebMCP capabilities.
what_it_does: Mentria exposes dozens of browser tools, games, extensions, and cross-tab capabilities to on-device AI and compatible agents.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP turns a broad, evolving toolbox into a discoverable shared capability bus, including cross-tab operations that generic UI driving would handle unreliably.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 34 tools, dynamic registration, read-only annotations, and cross-tab capability sharing.
Frames show multiple tool workspaces, launcher, consoles, and concrete outputs such as QR codes.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a broad but coherent product with multiple tools and visible outputs; breadth creates some uncertainty about completeness of every capability.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show repeated tool/configuration/output states and a launcher-like toolbox.
Devpost packaging presents on-device AI and WebMCP as an integrated product.
impact_rationale: Privacy-conscious users and developers can benefit from local models operating practical browser tools without sending core data away.
impact_evidence: About text states local WebGPU models up to 27B and no core data leaving the device.
Cross-tool multi-step tasks and user-installable extensions address real workflow needs.
creativity_rationale: The combination of on-device AI, a capability bus, cross-tab orchestration, and standard WebMCP access is an ambitious platform concept.
creativity_evidence: One bridge exposes an entire extensible site to both local and external agents.
Multi-step tasks can be compressed into a single WebMCP call.
usability_note: Many tools and developer-oriented surfaces may increase discoverability and learning burden.
red_flags: Very broad scope makes depth and reliability of all 34 tools hard to verify.
advance_reason: Platform-level leverage and meaningful privacy-oriented impact.

one_line: A browser conformance suite that exposes silent WebMCP behavior drops with reproducible probes.
what_it_does: Ninth Tool runs twenty WebMCP behavior probes in a real browser and reports gaps with commands, findings, and dynamic inspection tools.
leverage_rationale: The product specifically makes browser behavior and WebMCP contract failures observable and reproducible; a general UI agent cannot substitute for deterministic conformance probing.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 20 probes, two transports, reproduction commands, and dynamic findings tooling.
Frames show dense multi-column test/report interfaces with code-like rows and statuses.
execution_rationale: The stated scope is unusually concrete and the frame sheets show a substantial, structured audit/report product with live and headless modes.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show long behavior catalogs, test rows, code snippets, and status-like results.
About text reports a specific 13 broken/5 kept/1 by design/1 unsettled audit and a headless CLI runner.
impact_rationale: WebMCP implementers need to know whether browser promises are honored; reproducible diagnostics can prevent silent correctness and safety failures.
impact_evidence: About text identifies destructiveHint, error envelopes, and signals being silently dropped.
No-account Chrome/Edge compatibility and MIT code support practical adoption.
creativity_rationale: Turning protocol ambiguity into an executable, twenty-behavior conformance catalogue is a sharp and original developer-tool concept.
creativity_evidence: Dynamic tool mutation and paired browser/headless transports extend beyond a static checker.
Every behavior is tied to a reproduction command.
usability_note: Reports and exact reproductions are useful to technical users, though dense diagnostics may intimidate newcomers.
red_flags: Small frame text prevents independent verification of individual probe labels.
standouts: Reproducible findings rather than generic claims.
advance_reason: One of the clearest and most indispensable WebMCP projects in the packet.

one_line: A parent-child learning board where an AI tutor works alongside a Grade 2 student.
what_it_does: Fun Lab Kids maps NC Grade 2 standards into interactive math, ELA, and science labs with progress, rewards, and agent-assisted board actions.
leverage_rationale: An agent can manipulate the same visible learning board, run checks, and suggest next steps, which is materially better than a separate chat but still replicable with some UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text names tools for opening labs, moving pieces, checking answers, hints, and suggestions.
Frames show activity, form, scoreboard, and progress states.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent educational app with multiple labs, progress states, and a consistent visual system, but no legible end-to-end agent trace.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show welcome, scoreboard/setup, activity, and progress-like states.
About text specifies three main labs and 77 mapped standards.
impact_rationale: Parents and young learners have a concrete need for aligned, understandable homework help; shared-board tutoring directly addresses the stated disconnect.
impact_evidence: About text grounds the product in NC Grade 2 materials and a parent-child tutoring problem.
No account and local progress support a family-oriented use case.
creativity_rationale: The shared board where the child remains in control while an agent moves pieces and checks work is a thoughtful interaction model, not merely chat tutoring.
creativity_evidence: Human confirmation is required for major moves.
Learning, game rewards, and agent collaboration are integrated into one board.
usability_note: Colorful activity and progress flows appear approachable for children, though the breadth of standards may create navigation complexity.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not visibly prove agent invocation.
advance_reason: High impact and strong concept despite limited direct invocation evidence.

one_line: A cockpit that visualizes an AI agent's predicted blast radius before changes land.
what_it_does: TREMOR presents dependency graphs, risk indicators, and systemic regression findings for agent-driven code changes.
leverage_rationale: Structured impact analysis gives an agent and human a shared dependency/risk state that is difficult to obtain reliably by navigating ordinary UI.
leverage_evidence: About text frames the product as a browser-native WebMCP safety cockpit.
Frames show dependency graphs with green/orange/red risk states and expanded findings panels.
execution_rationale: The visual system and repeated graph/risk states are coherent, but the packet does not clearly demonstrate the underlying analysis workflow end to end.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show many cockpit states with color-coded graph nodes and critical findings.
Devpost image visibly promotes a 79% critical-risk state.
impact_rationale: Engineering teams have a real need to detect cross-service consequences of autonomous changes before deployment; the proposed safety layer addresses that risk.
impact_evidence: About text gives a concrete architectural-myopia and cache-stampede scenario.
Frames show systemic dependency and severity visualization.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to preflight agent change impact and presenting a blast-radius cockpit is a fresh, timely developer-safety concept.
creativity_evidence: Explicit AI-specific change-failure framing.
Shared visual risk cockpit rather than a generic agent chat.
usability_note: Color coding and cockpit framing are legible, but dense dependency graphs likely require technical expertise.
red_flags: Promotional risk number is not independently tied to a readable invocation.
Exact analysis inputs and validation are unclear.
standouts: Strong safety-oriented framing for autonomous coding agents.
advance_reason: Credible and impactful agent-safety product with good visual evidence.

one_line: A visual editor that lets agents design pixel-perfect embedded-display GUIs and generate code.
what_it_does: Lopaka provides a canvas, layers, assets, target configuration, preview, and code generation for microcontroller displays, now exposed through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Structured inspection and editing of layers, assets, target sizes, and generated code is useful, but a competent agent could achieve much of the same through ordinary editor UI with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for inspecting/editing canvas state, layers, assets, and generated code.
Frames show an editor progressing from blank canvas to a Home Air dashboard.
execution_rationale: The editor and generated artifact are visibly coherent, with a clear path from design surface to a recognizable embedded dashboard.
execution_evidence: Frames show blank/editor states, iterative processing overlays, and final HOME AIR | LIVE dashboard with rooms and CO2.
Devpost screenshot embeds the finished dashboard and identifies an AI Agents with WebMCP demo.
impact_rationale: Embedded developers and designers have a real need for visual, pixel-accurate constrained-display authoring and code generation.
impact_evidence: About text explicitly positions Lopaka as Figma for embedded displays.
Visible result includes room cards and CO2 display appropriate to a small-device GUI.
creativity_rationale: The embedded-display design workflow is a strong niche synthesis, though the underlying visual-editor category is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent-accessible pixel-perfect constrained hardware design.
Asset search, layer editing, and code generation are pursued together.
usability_note: Visual canvas plus live preview should be approachable, though embedded target configuration adds complexity.
red_flags: The project predates the challenge and WebMCP was added during submission; assess contribution accordingly.
advance_reason: Solid execution and audience fit with meaningful, if not transformative, WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A plain-language legal information portal for people trying to understand everyday rights and next steps.
what_it_does: Justice Compass lets users describe legal problems naturally, structure facts and evidence, find relevant law, and prepare possible next steps.
leverage_rationale: Natural-language intake and structured legal-information retrieval are useful WebMCP capabilities, but the same broad outcome could be approximated by an agent driving a conventional portal.
leverage_evidence: About text describes tools for structuring problems, organizing facts, and finding relevant legal information.
Frames show a polished legal landing page but no legible tool surface.
execution_rationale: The submission presents a coherent visual identity and claimed workflow, but frame sheets mostly show landing-page variants and do not demonstrate the core legal flow end to end.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show repeated dark legal-portal landing/content states.
Devpost page provides a project description and demo preview.
impact_rationale: People facing everyday disputes are a real audience with a serious access-to-understanding problem; plain-language guidance and next-step organization can provide substantial value.
impact_evidence: About text grounds the problem in Uganda and ordinary people struggling with legal terminology and actionability.
Product explicitly avoids claiming to replace lawyers or provide definitive representation.
creativity_rationale: Accessible legal explanation is valuable but the interaction model appears closer to a conventional guided legal-information assistant than a novel medium-specific concept.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language problem intake and plain-language law framing.
WebMCP integration is claimed but not visibly demonstrated.
usability_note: The dark/yellow visual system and plain-language promise are clear, but the legal workflow is not visible enough to judge fully.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not show the claimed core legal analysis workflow.
No public repository and no direct invocation evidence in the packet.
advance_reason: High potential impact, but core execution and WebMCP evidence are too thin for advancement.

one_line: An agent-native procurement marketplace that requires human approval before spending.
what_it_does: Procura lets an agent search and compare workplace equipment, render judgments in the shared UI, prepare an order, and poll an explicit human approval state.
leverage_rationale: Shared product comparisons, provenance of who added items, asynchronous approval, and server-side enforcement make the human-agent procurement workflow substantially more reliable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies 25 tools, compare_products, approval request/check tools, and server-side refusal without approval.
Frames show sequential catalog, product, cart, and approval-panel states.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete central workflow and frame sheets visibly show catalog-to-cart-to-approval progression with modal gates.
execution_evidence: Four-panel motion collage shows browsing, product dialogs, cart/order summaries, and confirmation/approval states.
About text details asynchronous approval, audit fields, and dual enforcement layers.
impact_rationale: Workplace buyers and teams have a clear procurement problem: delegate research and comparison while retaining financial control; the solution directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text identify the agent-spend safety gap.
Shared comparison table and explicit approval panel visibly match the intended workflow.
creativity_rationale: The product deeply pursues a human-agent purchasing interaction in which the agent's judgment is rendered into the page and spending authority is structurally withheld.
creativity_evidence: Agent decisions appear as comparison-table judgments rather than opaque chat prose.
Server and tool layers both deny autonomous approval, with attribution for every cart/order action.
usability_note: The staged marketplace flow and explicit approval gate are understandable and appropriately safety-conscious.
red_flags: Underlying calls are not readable in the frame sheets, though state transitions are strong evidence.
standouts: Agent reasoning rendered into shared UI.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage, execution, impact, and creativity with unusually strong safety boundaries.

one_line: A conversational academic planner that builds conflict-free schedules without enrolling the student.
what_it_does: The advisor reads a transcript, checks prerequisites and seats, proposes schedules, balances workload, tracks degree requirements, and lets students revise alternatives conversationally.
leverage_rationale: Agent access to transcript, catalog, prerequisites, seats, timetable, and degree audit creates a shared planning workflow that is markedly more reliable than manually navigating many registrar pages.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies transcript reading, prerequisite/seat checks, schedule construction, swaps, and degree-audit views.
Frames show structured multi-panel planning/result interfaces, though text is small.
execution_rationale: The claimed scope is coherent and the packet shows substantial planning/data surfaces, but core end-to-end scheduling evidence and readable tool calls are limited.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show repeated structured tables, panels, forms, and result-like states.
Devpost page includes a dedicated course-advisor demo video and clear workflow description.
impact_rationale: University students face a real, recurring course-planning problem; conflict avoidance, graduation visibility, and workload tradeoffs offer direct value.
impact_evidence: About text grounds the audience in Bucknell students and hundreds of available courses.
Draft/no-seats-held banner and user-controlled enrollment address a consequential usability risk.
creativity_rationale: Conversational schedule planning with a live timetable and degree audit is a fresh synthesis, though academic planning itself is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language preference changes update alternatives rather than rebuilding manually.
Draft schedule remains visibly distinct from enrolled courses.
usability_note: The draft-versus-enrolled distinction and visible timetable support safe planning, though the amount of academic data may be dense.
red_flags: Frames are too small to verify exact course results or invocation details.
advance_reason: High audience value and meaningful structured-agent planning leverage.
